quiz.q: Why does the WTO's formal consensus rule fail to protect developing countries from unfavourable trade outcomes in practice?
options: Major powers use informal Green Room diplomacy to pressure developing nations into falling in line.
Voting shares are formally weighted by each member state's total contribution to global merchandise trade.
Developing countries are legally prohibited from casting a veto against proposals introduced by developed nations.
Decisions are strictly determined through majority voting, marginalising countries with smaller populations and lower GDP.
quiz.why: Although every member formally possesses veto power, developed nations use exclusive Green Room negotiations to pressure developing states into accepting agreements.

quiz.q: Why is India's Minimum Support Price (MSP) food procurement challenged under WTO agricultural rules?
options: The WTO classifies all state-backed food distribution networks as prohibited export subsidies.
Procurement incentives count as Amber Box subsidies and risk breaching the ten percent de minimis limit.
Agricultural price support is categorised as a Blue Box measure that illegally mandates production-limiting quotas.
Subsidies for food grain procurement are permitted only when calculated against real-time global inflation rates.
quiz.why: MSP is classified as a trade-distorting Amber Box domestic subsidy, which for developing countries cannot exceed ten percent of agricultural production value based on 1986-88 prices.

quiz.q: What is the primary divide between developed countries and India regarding the four modes of services trade?
options: Developed nations champion Mode One cross-border delivery, while India completely opposes digital commerce and outsourcing.
Developed nations demand free consumption abroad under Mode Two, while India seeks to restrict tourist travel.
Developed nations champion Mode Three commercial presence, but resist India's push for Mode Four professional mobility.
India demands liberalising Mode Three banking presence, while developed nations push for unrestricted Mode Four immigration.
quiz.why: Developed countries aggressively pursue Mode III commercial presence in banking and insurance, while restricting Mode IV visas for the movement of Indian professionals.

quiz.q: What is the central disagreement between India and the United States over the Special Safeguard Mechanism (SSM)?
options: The maximum duration emergency tariff duties can remain imposed on subsidised agricultural commodity imports.
Whether safeguard mechanisms should cover industrial manufactured goods rather than domestic agricultural produce.
Whether safeguard duties must be refunded to exporting countries once international commodity prices stabilize.
The import surge threshold required before a country can raise tariffs to protect domestic farmers.
quiz.why: India maintains that a modest import surge should trigger safeguard duties to protect subsistence farmers, whereas the United States insists on a substantial surge threshold.
